guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / spinal injury and helmet removal
title: Helmet removal after a BMX crash
setting: BMX track. Rider crashed jump, landed badly on head and shoulder. Sore/stiff neck, wearing helmet, unresponsive/vomited.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive patient with a compromised airway (vomiting while unresponsive), wearing a helmet, and high risk of spinal injury. Sick: immediate airway protection.

shared.danger: BMX track uneven ground and spectators
shared.airway: Clear and speaking in full sentences
shared.circulation: Slight bruising on shoulder, skin is pale

er.exposure: Outside, wearing helmet and protective clothing

history.history: Injured after coming off a jump at speed, hit shoulder and head 5 minutes ago
history.injuries: Helmet still in place, dizziness, neck pain, nausea

followUp.question: What is the priority management step for this patient?

options.text: Stabilize the head and spine in a neutral position, call 999, and safely remove the helmet using a two-person technique if breathing is threatened
Pull the helmet off immediately to relieve pressure on the neck
Encourage him to stand up and walk to the nearest first aid tent
Do nothing; wait for the ambulance crew to arrive before touching the patient

followUp.explanation: Suspected spinal injury. Stabilize the head and spine in a neutral position. Call 999 immediately. Only remove the helmet if breathing is threatened or if the airway is compromised (e.g. vomiting), using a safe two-person technique. Never pull the helmet off immediately or allow walking.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999. Stabilize head and spine. Reassure patient, keep warm.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected spinal injury. Maintain neutral alignment. Check BGL, monitor vitals. If patient goes unresponsive and vomits, safely remove helmet using two-person technique, clear airway, and place in recovery position using log-roll.
